rule: These are research targets, not supported vehicles. Nothing here is marked verified: a request being sent, a catalog row existing, or a test passing does not make a feature supported.
sources: Counts describe the catalog bundled in this app version (DtcCatalog.sqlite: opendbc, OVMS, OBDb and others) plus the app's own code and JSON files. They are third-party references until a real-vehicle capture is reviewed.

coverage.genericObd2: Applies to any SAE J1979 car; not verified for this model.
coverage.moduleScanFamily: Nissan family. The module scan asks 7 hard-coded candidate addresses (ABS 0x740, SRS 0x752, BCM 0x745, cluster 0x743, EPS 0x742, HVAC 0x744, key 0x746) plus catalog candidates filtered by brand, not by model. A candidate is only reported if the car answers.
coverage.notes: The 4 catalog ECU rows (platform Altima 2019-24, opendbc firmware-query addresses): engine 0x7E0, EPS 0x742, forward camera 0x707, gateway 0x18DAD0F1. They are request addresses only, with no response IDs, services or decoding. The oil-control reset is a manual procedure from the owner's manual; no diagnostic reset routine is known.

targets.adapterNotes: Generic OBD-II and the existing read-only module scan can be tried with the existing adapter. The 0x18DAD0F1 gateway row is a 29-bit address; the scan treats any address above 0x7FF as 29-bit, and whether the adapter can reach it on an 11-bit OBD car is not established. One scan asks at most 48 candidate addresses.
missing: Response IDs and documented read-only services for ABS, SRS, BCM, cluster and HVAC (the 7 probe addresses are unverified candidates).
DTC status format used by those modules.
Model-year coverage: catalog addresses are for 2019-24 only.
Any capture from a real vehicle.
vehicleConditions: Write down the model year; the catalog data is for 2019-24.

coverage.genericObd2: Applies to any SAE J1979 car; not verified for this model.
coverage.moduleScanFamily: Stellantis family (Opel is grouped with Peugeot, Citroen and DS), not GM. There is no hard-coded probe table for it. The scan asks the standard addresses plus catalog rows for PSA/Stellantis and Fiat (520 rows, brand-filtered, at most 48 candidates per scan). Those rows come from PSA-vehicle data and are only candidates for an Astra: Astras of the GM era and of the Stellantis era are different designs, and this app does not establish which applies. The GM North America probe table is not used for Opel.

A candidate is only reported if the car answers. One scan asks at most 48 candidate addresses, so many of those rows may never be asked.

They are request addresses only. The service-interval reset is a research candidate (family.vag.sri-reset) that needs a model-specific DID mapping.

coverage.genericObd2: Not established. There is no evidence in this project that a Model 3 answers SAE J1979 requests through an ELM327.
coverage.moduleScanFamily: None. Tesla is not a recognised brand family in the module scan.
coverage.notes: The catalog has one ECU row (EPS 0x730, opendbc) and CAN signal descriptions: 209 and 240 signals for two Model 3 DBC files, plus 572 and 74 in two general Tesla files. These describe messages broadcast on Tesla's own CAN buses, not diagnostic requests. The OVMS Model 3 entry has no ECU addresses.

targets.adapterNotes: Public projects (opendbc, OVMS) read the Model 3 through its CAN buses with dedicated hardware, not with ELM327 diagnostic requests. This app has no evidence that an ELM327 gets any answer from a Model 3, so it is not claimed. If a capture shows no answer to 0100, the model is unsupported by this adapter path.

coverage.moduleScanFamily: GM family with a hard-coded candidate table (includes 0x7E2 TCM, 0x7E4 hybrid, 0x7E7 battery). A candidate is only reported if the car answers.
coverage.notes: The most developed target. The app already has a read-only battery reader (module 0x7E7 to 0x7EF, 96 cell-group identifiers, battery temperature 0x7E4 22 434F) and an oil-life DID 0x119F read path. The battery reader follows the community OBDb project, which marks the values it uses as confirmed on real cars; the oil-life DID is described in the app as research only. This project has not seen either on a real car. The tests use fixtures and the software simulator. The oil-life reset has no diagnostic routine; it is a manual procedure. The GM global DBC files in the catalog are generic GM, not Volt-specific.

targets.adapterNotes: The modules sit on standard-range OBD CAN IDs (0x7E4, 0x7E7), so the existing ELM327 path can be tried.
